setup.title: OTRS, Znuny and OTOBO setup
setup.step1: As admin, create an agent (Admin → Agents) named mcharbor with a strong password, and give it rw permission on the target queue's group (Admin → Agents ↔ Groups).
setup.step2: Create a customer user (Admin → Customer Users) for McHarbor tickets, or reuse an existing one, and note its login.
setup.step3: Create a Ticket dynamic field of type Text named McHarborDedupKey (Admin → Dynamic Fields). It does not need to be shown on any screen.
setup.step4: Copy the web service YAML for your product with a button below, then go to Admin → Web Services → Add Web Service → Import web service, and import it with the name McHarborConnectorREST. On OTRS 8 or later, keep only the Provider part.
setup.step5: In McHarbor, save this channel, edit it again, and under Ticket status from the ITSM select Create inbound URL. Copy the URL and its signing secret; both are shown once.
setup.step6: In the imported web service, open the requester transport HTTP::REST: set Host to your McHarbor base URL, the McHarborStateChanged controller to /api/incident-webhooks/, and the X-McHarbor-Webhook-Secret header to the secret.
setup.step7: Optional: on the McHarborStateChanged invoker's TicketStateUpdate event, add a condition that McHarborDedupKey is not empty so only McHarbor tickets are sent.
setup.step8: On OTRS 8 or later, or when you skip steps 5 to 7, keep the poll interval above 0 so McHarbor reads ticket state itself.
setup.step9: Click Test connection. It logs in, searches the queue and checks the dynamic field without creating a ticket.
